description: Applicants are routed to Ankara, Istanbul, Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Yerevan. Reporting suggests Ankara handles roughly 60% of Iranian J-1 cases with Abu Dhabi taking most of the rest.

aspect: The interview trip itself needs a visa
description: Turkey is visa-free for Iranians, which is why Ankara and Istanbul carry the volume. Armenia is visa-free. The UAE is not - a Dubai or Abu Dhabi interview requires a UAE visa first, an application that is itself frequently refused for young Iranian men.
notes: The UAE refusal pattern for young single Iranian men is widely reported in forums; no official statistic located.

aspect: Direct cost of a single interview trip
description: Flights and accommodation for one interview trip estimated at USD 800-1,500 on top of the USD 185 visa fee and, for students, the USD 220 SEVIS fee.

aspect: Repeat trips when documents are requested
description: Administrative processing often asks for further documents or a second interview, and the applicant has usually returned to Iran by then. Each round trip repeats the full cost.

Applicants who moved to Turkey or Armenia to be near a post must maintain legal residence there for months or years while the case sits. Residence permit refusal or expiry can collapse the whole application.
money_note: Rent and permit costs while waiting.
notes: Common pattern in Iranian applicant forums; deserves layer-5 research against real case accounts.

description: Omid flies Tehran-Yerevan for his interview: USD 320 return, three nights at USD 55. The officer takes his passport and issues a 221(g). Eleven weeks later the consulate emails asking for his military service card and a CV. He flies back to hand in two sheets of paper. Total for the second trip: USD 430. He has now spent more on travel than the visa fee, twice.
energy_note: Flying to another country to deliver a photocopy.
